title: Maximum Elegance of a K-Length Subsequence
summary: Given a 0-indexed 2D integer array items of length n and an integer k, you are to find the maximum elegance of a subsequence of size exactly k.
statement: Given a 0-indexed 2D integer array items of length n and an integer k, you are to find the maximum elegance of a subsequence of size exactly k. The elegance of a subsequence is defined as the total profit of the items in the subsequence plus the square of the number of distinct categories present in the subsequence. Return the highest elegance value that can be achieved by any subsequence of size k.
constraints: Each item is [positive profit, category]; choose exactly k items.
Elegance is total profit plus the square of distinct category count.
hints: Start with maximum profit, then trade only duplicate-category items for new categories.
Sort by profit, keep duplicate profits in a min-heap, and scan unused new categories.
Replace the cheapest duplicate and update profit+distinct² after each replacement.
For each achievable category count, the greedy exchange retains the greatest possible profit, so the best recorded elegance is global.

tests.explanation: Choosing profits ten and three yields profit thirteen with two categories, for elegance seventeen.
The best three-item choice balances high profit with a third category.
